title: RBACv2-KMS Bridge and SIEM Export Playbook
content:
Purpose: This playbook describes the integration points between RBACv2, the KMS/HSM stack, BYOK escrow and recovery processes, and the downstream SIEM export format for cryptographic events. Audience: security engineers, infra, SREs, platform.

High-level recommendations:
1) Use explicit RBACv2 role-to-KMS permission mapping (crypto-admin, key-operator, key-viewer, auditor, recovery-operator).
2) Emit structured audit events for all key lifecycle changes.
3) Create immutable evidence bundles on escrow, recovery, destroy, and root rotations and index bundle IDs in SIEM.
4) Implement a gated recovery bridge for BYOK with multi-approver workflow.

RBACv2 role mapping (summary):
- crypto-admin: full control over KMS metadata and root configurations.
- key-operator: manage key versions and trigger rewraps for tenant keys.
- key-viewer: metadata read-only.
- auditor: read-only access to audit streams and evidence bundles.
- recovery-operator: can execute BYOK recoveries after 2-of-3 approvals.

Policy guidance: represent mappings as RBACv2 constraints stored in a reconciler service; avoid baking roles into KMS code. Example policy lines (pseudocode style): grant crypto-admin -> resource:/kms/* action:all scope:org; grant key-operator -> resource:/kms/keys/{tenant} action:create,update,rewrap scope:tenant; grant auditor -> resource:/kms/audit/* action:read scope:org.

Audit event fields (every event must include these string fields): event_timestamp, event_type, key_id, key_version, actor_id, actor_roles, action_result, source_ip, request_id, tenant_id, seal_type, origin, correlation_id. Optional string-list fields: approval_ids. Optional string fields: justification, previous_key_version, metrics_summary.

Event example (compact, key=value pairs): event_timestamp=2025-02-12T18:03:21Z, event_type=escrow_recover, key_id=kms://us-east1/keys/tenanted-abc123, key_version=v5, actor_id=sec-ops:priya.n, actor_roles=[recovery-operator], action_result=success, source_ip=34.120.44.12, request_id=req-7f3e9a, tenant_id=tenant-42, seal_type=byok, origin=hosted, correlation_id=rollout-09, justification=customer requested key recovery under approved SRA-678, approval_ids=[SRA-678-A1,SRA-678-A2].

SIEM export patterns: send NDJSON with one audit event per line. Map fields: @timestamp <- event_timestamp; event.action <- event_type; event.outcome <- action_result; user.id <- actor_id; user.roles <- actor_roles; object.id <- key_id; organization.id <- tenant_id; add evidence.bundle_id when present. Use a broker (Vector or Logstash) to enrich with geoip and identity resolution and to attach correlation IDs. For batch-heavy operations emit both per-item events and a compact summary event with batch_id and counts to limit SIEM volume.

Evidence bundles: generated on escrow_onboard, escrow_recover, key_destroy, and root-level rotations. Bundle contents (textual description): audit NDJSON subset, approval artifacts (signed), KMS config snapshot, RBACv2 snapshot, redacted request traces, HSM attestation or thumbprint. Store bundles in immutable cloud storage with object lock and retention per contract (default 7 years). Record bundle_id in audit event so SIEM can link to stored evidence.

Key rotation and rewrap model: use envelope encryption. Tenant DEKs wrapped by KMS key versions; KEK stored in HSM. Rotation modes: version-rotate (create new version and mark primary, background rewrap), immediate-rewrap (incident-driven, bulk job). Background rewrap workers should be idempotent, rate-limited, and shard-aware. Keep old versions until no objects reference them or TTL expires.

BYOK onboarding & recovery bridge (checklist): pre-onboard: confirm contract and escrow requirements; create onboarding ticket; assign temporary auditor role. Onboard: secure upload of key material, preflight checks, generate signed escrow receipt, update tenant metadata. Recovery: create recovery request with justification, acquire 2-of-3 approvals, run recovery in controlled environment with ephemeral creds, capture evidence, and notify customer.

Emergency handling: on suspected compromise rotate KEK immediately, mark emergency rewrap, produce evidence package, and run forensic capture. All emergency operations require RBACv2 enforcement and approval logging. Tamper evidence must include HSM attestation when available.

Operational cadence: daily: scan for scheduled rotates, check pending approvals, verify SIEM pipeline, ensure evidence exports. Weekly: test recovery gate in staging. Monthly: reconcile RBACv2 mapping with KMS reconciler and publish drift report.

Open questions: Should we log DEK hashes for integrity checks? Define TTL for old key versions for Dedicated customers. Add cross-region attestation proof for DR.

Review notes: reviewers should pay particular attention to evidence retention defaults and the RBAC role granularity proposed. Legal sign-off required for default retention before finalizing.

Document history: drafted 2024-11-05 by Priya Natarajan; infra revisions 2024-12-18; SIEM schema update 2025-02-12.

End of playbook.
